description: SQL Server provider extensions for EFCore.ComplexIndexes — clustered, covering (INCLUDE), online-built, and fill-factor index options for complex type properties.
releaseNotes:
The last 5.x minor with a change of its own: the line refuses EF Core 11, whose successor is CodoMetis.EFCore.SchemaKit.SqlServer.

Changed answers

- Indexes: a unique complex index over nullable columns gets EF Core's IS NOT NULL filter, so rows without a value no longer collide. It admitted one such row and refused the second (#88 (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/issues/88), Upgrading (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/docs/upgrading.md#unique-indexes-over-nullable-columns-on-sql-server)).
- Indexes: an IncludeProperties(…) entry that names neither a property nor a column of the table fails at migrations add. When its property was removed, the migration dropped only the column, and failed at apply with Msg 5074 (#142 (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/issues/142), Upgrading (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/docs/upgrading.md#include-entries-must-name-a-column)).

Breaking

- Registration: UseSqlServerComplexIndexes(), AddSqlServerComplexIndexes() and the design-time registration dotnet ef runs throw InvalidOperationException on an EF Core major other than 10, naming CodoMetis.EFCore.SchemaKit for EF Core 11. EF Core 10 on .NET 11 keeps working (Upgrading (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/docs/upgrading.md#ef-core-11-is-refused-at-registration)).
- Indexes: on a database with a case-sensitive collation, complex index names that differ only in case fail at migrations add; rename one (Upgrading (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/docs/upgrading.md#rename-complex-index-names-that-differ-only-in-case)).

Changed

- Packaging: each package carries the version's section of its changelog as its NuGet release notes, which nuget.org's Release Notes tab and Visual Studio's Updates tab show.
- Packaging: the release notes, the README on nuget.org and the GitHub release link the documentation at the version's tag, so they keep describing the version they shipped with after main moves on to the next line.
- Packaging: the PostgreSQL and SQL Server packages depend on exactly their own version of EFCore.ComplexIndexes, and the core differ refuses a satellite of another version, naming both. Update the packages together: a 5.4.x satellite beside core 5.5.0 was refused as the core differ (#169 (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/issues/169)).

Fixed

- Indexes: a clustered complex index added in a later migration beside an existing one, and a complex index named like its table's primary key or a unique constraint, fail at migrations add, where they failed at apply (SQL Server (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/docs/sqlserver.md#deliberate-rejections)).
- Indexes: complex index names that differ only in case, from each other or from a native index, fail at migrations add, where they failed at apply because the default collation compares them without regard to case (Index names (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/README.md#single-column-index-on-a-complex-property)).
- Migrations: a complex index renamed away from a name that the same migration gives to another index applies, where it failed at apply because the renamed index still held the name. It is dropped before EF Core's operations and created after them (Index names (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/README.md#single-column-index-on-a-complex-property)).
- Migrations: changing the type, length or nullability of a column a complex index reads applies, an index renamed in the same migration included, where it failed with Msg 5074. The index is dropped before the ALTER COLUMN and created after it (SQL Server (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/docs/sqlserver.md)).

Full changelog: https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/src/EFCore.ComplexIndexes.SqlServer/CHANGELOG.md
